info.name: Books Store API 📚
info.description:
A simple RESTful API to manage books and authors, built with Node.js. It supports basic CRUD operations and allows searching books by publisher.

## ✨ Features

- Manage books and authors with full CRUD operations
    
- Filter books by publisher
    
- RESTful and well-structured endpoints
    
- Easy to set up and run

response.name: List books

request.description:
### Request

This endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve the details of a specific book identified by the provided ID.

#### Request Body
The request does not include a request body.

The endpoint URL should be constructed as follows:
```
{{baseDomain}}{{versionApi}}books/66d9bc24850c85afa9585162
```

### Response

Upon a successful request, the endpoint returns the details of the specified book in the response body. The response will include the following details:
- `title`: The title of the book.
- `author`: The author of the book.
- `publication_date`: The publication date of the book.
- `genre`: The genre of the book.
- Any other relevant information related to the specified book.

This endpoint makes an HTTP POST request to create a new book in the system. The request should include a JSON payload in the raw request body type with the following parameters:
- "title": (string) The title of the book.
- "publisher": (string) The name of the publisher.
- "price": (number) The price of the book.

### Request Body
- title (string): The title of the book.
- publisher (string): The name of the publisher.
- price (number): The price of the book.

#### Response
The response will include a message and details of the newly created book, including:
- "message": A status message.
- "book": An object containing the details of the newly created book, including:
  - "title": The title of the book.
  - "publisher": The name of the publisher.
  - "price": The price of the book.
  - "pages": The number of pages in the book.
  - "author": An object containing the details of the author, including:
    - "name": The name of the author.
    - "country": The country of the author.
    - "_id": The unique identifier of the author.
  - "_id": The unique identifier of the book.

# Update Book Details

This API endpoint is used to update the details of a specific book.

## Request

### Request URL

- `PUT` {{baseDomain}}{{versionApi}}books/670db7da1c8c84565b34f09f
    

### Request Body

- The request body should be in JSON format and include the following parameters:
    

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| title | String | The title of the book. |
| publisher | String | The name of the publisher of the book. |
| price | Number | The price of the book. |

Example:

``` json
{
  "title": "Sample Title",
  "publisher": "Sample Publisher",
  "price": 25.99
}
## Response
The response for this request will be a JSON object conforming to the following schema:
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "status": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "message": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  }
}

 ```

# Get Authors

This endpoint retrieves a list of authors.

### Request

- Method: GET
    
- URL: `{{baseDomain}}{{versionApi}}authors`
    

### Response

The response will contain an array of author objects, where each author object includes the following fields:

- `_id` (string): The unique identifier of the author.
    
- `name` (string): The name of the author.
    
- `country` (string): The country of the author.
    

Example response body:

``` json
[
    {
        "_id": "",
        "name": "",
        "country": ""
    }
]

 ```
